name: GamerPlug
tagline: Swipe-to-match app for finding gaming teammates · no more randoms

pricing.notes: Free to download on iOS and Android; no paid tier published as of 2026-08-06.

verdictSummary: The software is one-shottable: swipeable profiles, mutual-match logic, and realtime chat are a session of Supabase work. The product is not the software; it is the pool of real, verified gamers on the other side of the swipe, across 20+ titles, with moderation keeping bots and fake profiles out. A matchmaking app with nobody on it matches nobody.
coreLoopDIY: Swipeable player cards filtered by game, rank, and region, with mutual-match reveal and a simple chat thread.
requirements: a gaming circle willing to actually join
whatYouLose: a liquid pool of players to match with
native iOS/Android apps with push notifications
discovery of strangers beyond your own circle
whyPeopleStillPay: It is free, so the honest question is why people install it instead of building their own: a matchmaker is worth exactly as much as who is on it. GamerPlug's job is aggregating real players across many games and keeping the pool clean of bots, and no weekend build inherits that pool.
notes: The rare free entry: the network moat argument with zero pricing noise.
prompt:
Build me a small looking-for-group matchmaker like GamerPlug, for my own gaming
circle rather than strangers. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3, server-rendered EJS plus htmx, no build
  step; one database file at data/lfg.db.
- Invite-only: an /admin page (password from .env) mints invite codes; a code
  plus a gamertag creates a profile, and a signed cookie remembers you.
- Profiles: gamertag, Discord handle, region, mic yes/no, and up to five games
  each with rank and preferred mode.
- Core loop: /browse deals one candidate card at a time, filtered to shared
  games and region, with Plug and Skip buttons; a mutual Plug is a match.
- A match reveals both Discord handles and opens a message thread that
  refreshes via htmx polling every few seconds; no websockets.
- A /matches page lists your matches with the last message preview.
- No accounts beyond the invite cookie, no telemetry; binds to localhost
  unless you put it behind your own reverse proxy.
- Out of scope: native apps, stranger discovery, verification, tournaments,
  and leaderboards; the point is matching people already one invite away.
- README: setup, minting invites, and a one-line warning that a matchmaker is
  only as good as how many friends you invite.
